name: create_alert
title: Create Alert
description:
Creates an alert with a single condition on an instrument's price, volume, percent change, fee rate, or shortable shares — or on the caller's account margin cushion or daily P&L.
Returns the new alert's id.
Platform limitation: Alerts created via this tool are currently only visible and manageable in IBKR Desktop.
They will not appear in IBKR Mobile, TWS, or Client Portal.
Always tell the user this before creating an alert, so they aren't surprised when it doesn't show up outside Desktop.
If no email is provided, the user is notified only in IBKR Desktop when the alert triggers and receives no notification otherwise (no push, no SMS, no other email).
Before calling this tool without an email parameter, confirm with the user that they intend to rely on in-app-only notification, or ask if they would like to supply an email.

symbol.description: Display name for the alert, typically the symbol (e.g. "AAPL"). Cosmetic only — does not affect evaluation.

contract_id.description: Contract identifier from search_contracts (underlying_contract_id). Not restricted to a specific security type. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted. Required unless condition_type is MARGIN_CUSHION or DAILY_PNL.

exchange.description:
Exchange on which the alert condition is evaluated.
Pass SMART, or any exchange the contract trades on (from search_contracts).
Not used when condition_type is MARGIN_CUSHION or DAILY_PNL.

condition_type.description:
Which market value — or account metric — the condition tracks.
Supported condition types (values for the 'condition_type' input field):
 - LAST: Last trade price.
 - BID_ASK: Bid/ask price.
 - DOUBLE_BID_ASK: Average of the bid and ask price (double bid/ask).
 - DOUBLE_LAST: Double last price.
 - LAST_OR_BID_ASK: Either the last trade price or the bid/ask price, whichever crosses first.
 - MID_POINT: Midpoint between the current bid and ask.
 - VOLUME: Today's total trading volume.
 - PERCENT_CHANGE: Percent change from the prior session close.
 - SHORTABLE_SHARES: Number of shares available to short.
 - FEE_RATE: Short borrow fee rate.
 - MARGIN_CUSHION: The caller's current account margin cushion. Account-level — does not use contract_id/exchange.
 - DAILY_PNL: The caller's current account daily P&L. Account-level — does not use contract_id/exchange.
Units of `value`: for LAST, BID_ASK, DOUBLE_BID_ASK, DOUBLE_LAST, LAST_OR_BID_ASK, and MID_POINT, value is a raw price (e.g. 200 for $200).
For VOLUME, a share count.
For SHORTABLE_SHARES, a share count.
For PERCENT_CHANGE and FEE_RATE, a percentage rate (e.g. 5 for 5%).
For MARGIN_CUSHION and DAILY_PNL, value must be a percentage — there is no dollar-amount option for these condition types.
If the user gives a threshold in dollars (e.g. "alert me if I'm down $50 today" or "alert me if my margin cushion falls below $50"), do not convert or pass it through as-is.
Tell the user that MARGIN_CUSHION and DAILY_PNL alerts only support percentage thresholds, and ask them to restate the threshold as a percentage.

operator.description:
Comparison operator applied to value.
 - GTE: fires when the tracked value becomes >= value (e.g. "alert me when AAPL goes above $200" is GTE with value 200).
 - LTE: fires when the tracked value becomes <= value.

value.description: Trigger value. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted.

active_hours.description: Active hours. Possible options: REGULAR, EXTENDED, OVERNIGHT, ALL

tif.description: How long the alert stays active. UNTIL_TRIGGERED (default), UNTIL_DATE (requires expiry_date), or UNTIL_DELETED.

expiry_date.description: Date the alert expires, as a date-only ISO-8601 string (e.g. "2023-05-27") — no time component and no timezone. Required when tif is UNTIL_DATE.

email.description: Email address to notify when the alert triggers.Strongly recommended — without this, notification is limited to IBKR Desktop only, with no other alerting mechanism (no push, no SMS, no email)

email_note.description: Note prepended to the alert email body.

name: delete_alert
title: Delete Alert
description:
Permanently deletes one or more alerts. This action is irreversible.
Confirm with the user before calling.
Call get_alerts first to find the ids of the alerts to delete.

ids.description: Alert identifiers to delete, from get_alerts.

name: get_alert
title: Get Alert
description:
Returns the full detail of one alert: id, name, status, expiry_date, tif, email, email_note, and condition (contract_id, exchange, condition_type, operator, value).
Call get_alerts first to find the id of the alert to inspect.
Call this before update_alert — update_alert is a full-replace PUT, so you need the current settings to avoid clearing fields you didn't mean to change.

name: get_alerts
title: Get Alerts
description:
Returns a summary of the user's alerts.
Status is ACTIVE or PAUSED (set via set_alert_status)
Deleted alerts no longer appear in results.
Call get_alert for the full detail of a specific alert.

name: set_alert_status
title: Set Alert Status
description:
Pauses or resumes one or more alerts without deleting them.
Call get_alerts first to find the ids of the alerts to update.

action.description: PAUSE to deactivate, RESUME to reactivate.

name: update_alert

name: search_contracts
title: Search Contracts
description:
Search for contracts (instruments) by ticker symbol, company name, or keyword and return
        matching instruments with their contract identifiers (contract_id), exchanges, symbols,
        and available security-type sections. Returns the contract_id required by
        get_company_themes and get_company_connections — call this first to resolve a contract_id
        whenever you only have a company name or ticker.
        Each result row includes a sections array listing the security types available for that instrument (e.g. STK, OPT, FUT).
        When selecting a row for options: the primary selector is an EXACT match on the `symbol` field (e.g. for root "AAPL" select only the row where symbol == "AAPL", not "AAPU", "AAPB", etc.); having OPT in sections is necessary but NOT sufficient on its own, because many leveraged/income ETFs also carry OPT sections. When multiple rows with the exact symbol remain, prefer the primary listing using the `description` and `country_code` fields to disambiguate (e.g. the US primary listing rather than a foreign listing). Use the `underlying_contract_id` of the selected row for subsequent calls.

query.description: Ticker symbol, company name, or keyword to search for.

language.description: Language parameter. Supported values: ar, cs_CZ, de_DE, en_US, es_ES, et_EE, fr, he, hu_HU, it_IT, ja_JP, ko_KR, lt_LT, nl_NL, pl_PL, pt_BR, pt_PT, ru_RU, sl_SL, tr_TR, zh_CN, zh_TW. If a value is not in the list, omit the parameter entirely.

name: get_combo_identifier
title: Get Combo Identifier
description:
Creates a combo contract identifier from EQUITY OPTION (OPT) legs only.

Only OPT–OPT combos are supported. Every leg must be a standard
equity/index option (security type OPT) from an OPT option chain. Futures
options (FOP), futures (FUT), stocks (STK), and any mixed-type combination are
NOT supported and will fail when passed to create_order_instruction. Do NOT
call this tool with FOP legs. If the user wants a futures-options spread, tell
them multi-leg FOP combos aren't supported and offer to place each leg as a
separate single-leg FOP order via create_order_instruction instead.

Use this before create_order_instruction when placing a spread or multi-leg
options strategy.
Each leg requires a `contract_id_ex` (pass call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from
get_option_data verbatim) and a `size` (positive integer for BUY legs, negative for
SELL legs).
Returns a `contract_id_ex` string that identifies the combo — pass it directly to
create_order_instruction as contract_id_ex.
The response also includes a `description` (human-readable strategy summary) and
`strategy_name` (e.g. "Bull", "Combo").

legs.description:
List of option legs. Each leg has:
  contract_id_ex — full contract identifier, pass call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex
                   from get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "832609990@SMART").
                   Each leg's contract_id_ex must come from an OPT (equity option) chain returned
                   by get_option_data. FOP (futures option) contract ids are not valid here and
                   will fail downstream.
  size           — positive for BUY, negative for SELL (e.g. 1 or -1)
Pass size as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 1 or -1, not "1".

name: get_option_data
title: Get Option Data
description:
Returns the option chain for one expiration: a row per strike with `strike`, `call_contract_id_ex`, `call_contract_id`, `call_description`, `put_contract_id_ex`, `put_contract_id`, and `put_description`. The `*_description` strings carry option contract details such as expiration, strike and futures options include the contract multiplier in parentheses (e.g. '(50)' for ES, '(20)' for NQ). Use these when presenting a contract to the user. The response also contains a top-level `currency` field (e.g. "USD") and a top-level `exchange` field (e.g. "SMART") for the contracts in the chain.
Works for both equity options and futures options — the security type is inherited from the get_option_parameters call that produced the `expiration_id`.
This tool returns contract structure only — it does NOT return prices, implied volatility, open interest, or volume.
To obtain those, call get_price_snapshot using the numeric call_contract_id or put_contract_id together with the response's top-level exchange field.
Before choosing a range, fetch the underlying's spot price via get_price_snapshot and center min_strike/max_strike around it. Use a range wide enough to include at least 5 strikes on each side of the spot price in a single call.
Omitting all strike bounds on a liquid name can return hundreds of rows — always bound the range unless the user explicitly wants the full chain.
`expiration_id` must be a value taken verbatim from expirations[].id returned by get_option_parameters — never construct it.
call_contract_id_ex and put_contract_id_ex are the full contract identifiers (e.g. "832609990@SMART" for equity/index options, or "@CME" suffix for futures options). Pass these verbatim to create_order_instruction (as contract_id_ex) for single-leg OPT or FOP orders under REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow. For AUTONOMOUS live-order tools, only single-leg OPT ids from an OPT option chain are supported; never use FOP ids or combo/spread ids for submit_order, modify_order, preview_order, or get_order_rules. Only OPT (equity option) ids may be passed to get_combo_identifier — FOP ids are not valid combo legs. Use the numeric call_contract_id and put_contract_id together with the top-level exchange for get_price_snapshot / get_price_history (with security_type="OPT" or "FOP").
Note: each row's `strike` is returned as a STRING (e.g. "292.5") even though min_strike/max_strike inputs are numbers — cast `strike` to a number before performing numeric comparisons or arithmetic.
call_contract_id_ex/put_contract_id_ex and expiration IDs are internal identifiers used for chaining tool calls. Never display them to the user. Present results using symbol, expiry date, strike and exchange.

expiration_id.description:
Expiration identifier from get_option_parameters (expirations[].id).
Pass the value verbatim — do not construct it.

min_strike.description:
Optional lower bound on strike price.
Supply to limit response size (e.g. min_strike=185.0).
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted.

max_strike.description:
Optional upper bound on strike price.
Supply to limit response size (e.g. max_strike=195.0).
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted.

name: get_option_parameters
title: Get Option Parameters
description:
Returns available option expirations and the exchange list for an underlying.
The response includes an `exchanges` array of valid option exchanges and `current_exchange` (the preferred/default exchange).
Each expiration has: `id` (pass to get_option_data), `date` (YYYYMMDD), `regular` (true = standard monthly, false = weekly or daily/zero-days-to-expiration), and `trading_class` (present on every expiration row).
`current_expiration` is the id of the preferred (first regular) expiration.
For equity options (option_sec_type="OPT", default): call search_contracts and use the `underlying_contract_id` of the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include OPT.
For future options (option_sec_type="FOP"): call search_contracts and use the `underlying_contract_id` of the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include FOP.
Call this before get_option_data to resolve an expiration id.
Duplicate-date handling: never disambiguate expirations by `date` alone — always key on `id` which is unique.
A single `date` can carry multiple `trading_class` values that are DISTINCT contracts.
Always prefer expiration without `trading_class` or ask user to specify one. This occurs for both equity options (e.g. 'TSLA' and '2TSLA', 'NVDA' and '2NVDA') and futures options, where a date carries a quarterly class (e.g. 'ES', 'NQ') alongside weekly classes (e.g. 'EW3', 'QN3').
Contract IDs and expiration IDs are internal identifiers used for chaining tool calls.
Never display them to the user.
Present results using expiry date and exchange.

underlying_contract_id.description:
Contract id of the underlying.
For equity options: call search_contracts and use the `underlying_contract_id` of the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include OPT.
For future options: call search_contracts and use the `underlying_contract_id` of the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include FOP.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 265598.

option_exchange.description:
Limit results to a specific option exchange.
When not specified - default exchange will be picked and provided in response.
Additionally, `exchanges` array returned provides all availabe option exchanges.

option_sec_type.description: Security type of the options. Must be one of: "OPT" (standard equity/index options, default) or "FOP" (futures options).

name: search_futures
title: Search Futures
description:
Returns the futures term structure (the full expiry ladder) for a given underlying instrument.
The response is an object with a contracts array; each element has contract_id_ex, contract_id (numeric), exchange, contract_month (YYYYMM), last_trading_date (YYYYMMDD), and symbol.
Use contract_id_ex verbatim for create_order_instruction under REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow only. AUTONOMOUS live-order tools support STK and single-leg OPT only; never pass futures contract ids to submit_order, modify_order, preview_order, or get_order_rules. Futures contract ids are not valid get_combo_identifier legs.
Each contract also includes a numeric contract_id field and a separate exchange field — pass those directly to get_price_snapshot / get_price_history.
The `symbol` field is identical for every expiry rather than a per-contract code; it cannot be used to distinguish contracts and must never be displayed to the user. Identify and present an expiry using `contract_month` / `last_trading_date`.
Results are NOT returned in expiry order — sort by contract_month ascending yourself; the earliest non-expired entry is the front-month contract. This earliest entry can be within days of its `last_trading_date` and about to roll; when the user wants the actively-traded contract, the next expiry may be more appropriate.
To get underlying_contract_id, call search_contracts with the root symbol (optionally security_type=FUT), then take the underlying_contract_id field from the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include FUT.
Only active contracts are returned unless include_expired=true.

underlying_contract_id.description:
Contract id of the underlying instrument whose futures you want, obtained from search_contracts (use the underlying_contract_id field of the matching row, not a per-expiry futures contract id).
Pick the row whose symbol exactly matches the root and whose sections include FUT.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 530965695.

representative_only.description:
Defaults to true: returns only the single most representative (typically the standard, most-liquid) contract per expiry.
Set to false to return all listed contracts per expiry — use false when you need every variant or the complete raw ladder. For futures that list a single contract per expiry (e.g. equity-index futures such as ES and NQ), false returns the same ladder as the default.
Pass as a JSON boolean (true/false), not the string "true"/"false".

include_expired.description:
Defaults to false (active, non-expired contracts only).
Set true to also include expired contracts, e.g. for historical/backtest work.
Pass as a JSON boolean (true/false), not the string "true"/"false".

name: get_earnings_insight
title: Get Earnings Insight
description:
Retrieve a full earnings preview or recap using an id returned by
search_earnings_insights. Never construct or guess an insight ID.
Includes earnings estimates/actuals, KPIs, themes, impacted companies and historical
earnings reactions. Preview may include analyst price targets and bull/base/bear outlook;
recap may include guidance, peer context, risk updates and source citations.
Sections depend on report type and availability; missing fields are not zero values.
Price scenario low/high/median values are fractional returns (0.05 means 5%), and index
is the trading-day offset from earnings. Historical reactions are not forecasts.

id.description: Insight ID returned verbatim by search_earnings_insights.

lang.description: Optional language tag, e.g. en or zh-CN. Falls back to the original if unavailable.

name: search_earnings_insights
title: Search Earnings Insights
description:
Find earnings previews (before reporting) and recaps (after reporting) for
one or more companies. Returns summaries and insight IDs, not full report bodies.
Resolve names or tickers with search_contracts first, or use contract IDs from positions.
Pass a returned id verbatim to get_earnings_insight to retrieve the full report.
Results are ordered by reporting date, newest first; recap precedes preview on ties.
The page size applies across all companies, not per company. Defaults: size=10, offset=0.
To scan all matches, increment offset by size until a short or empty page is returned.
Date bounds filter reporting dates: start is inclusive, end is exclusive.
An empty result means no matching available insights, not that no earnings are scheduled.

contract_ids.description: Nonempty list of positive company contract IDs from search_contracts or account positions. Pass JSON numbers, e.g. [4815747, 9939].

type.description: Filter to preview or recap; omit to include both.

start.description: Inclusive reporting-date lower bound in UTC, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z.

end.description: Exclusive reporting-date upper bound in UTC, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z.

size.description: Positive maximum results across all companies. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Nonnegative starting result index. Defaults to 0; increment by size to paginate.

lang.description: Optional language tag, e.g. en or zh-CN. Falls back to the original if unavailable.

name: provide_customer_feedback
title: Provide Customer Feedback
description:
Submits feature requests and customer feedback.
Call this tool when
(1) the user wants brokerage functionality not yet offered by IBKR tools e.g. portfolio rebalance, funding and position transfers, dividends, screeners, and alike.
(2) you identify the user's sentiment towards or issues with IBKR's tools.
Always show the user the exact feedback_text you intend to submit and get their confirmation before calling.

feedback_text.description: Text of the customer feedback to submit

name: get_flow_type
title: Get Flow Type
description:
Returns this session's flow type: AUTONOMOUS or REVIEW_AND_APPROVE. Flow type is constant
for the session — call this once per session and reuse the cached result; it will
not change between calls.
RESULT:
- AUTONOMOUS: live-order placement is available only for STK (stocks) and
single-leg OPT (equity/index options). FUT, FOP, combos/spreads, and all other
security types cannot be placed through the live-order tools. See submit_order for
the full sequence.
- REVIEW_AND_APPROVE: submit_order, preview_order, get_order_rules,
get_order_status, answer_order_question, modify_order, and cancel_order are
unavailable; use create_order_instruction, delete_order_instruction, and
get_account_orders instead.
RULES: get_order_instructions and get_account_orders are not flow-restricted and
work under either flow type. Calling a flow-restricted tool under the wrong flow
type returns an error naming the correct tool for the current flow.

name: get_company_connections
title: Get Company Connections
description:
Return a company's competitors, products, and geographic exposure (countries and regions of operation).
Also includes sectors/trends but with supporting evidence explaining each connection.
Use when the user asks 'who are Pepsi's competitors', 'what does Tesla sell', 'where does Shell operate', or wants a full business overview.
Requires the company's contract_id — resolve with search_contracts first if you only have a name or ticker.
Relationship to get_company_themes: that tool is the lightweight choice when you only need sectors/trends + ranked peers.
Use get_company_connections for the broader profile (products/geography/competitors) or when you want evidence explaining WHY a connection exists.
To restrict to sectors/trends only, set link_types=['COMPANY_THEME'].

contract_id.description: Contract ID of the company, from search_contracts or get_theme_details. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 265598.

link_types.description:
Which connection types to return; omit for all. Use ['company_theme'] for themes,
['company_product'] for products, ['company_country']/['company_region'] for
geography, ['company_competitor'] for competitors. The company_* edges are anchored
on the company you pass; the inverse edges (theme_company, fund_theme, theme_fund)
traverse from a theme or fund and are generally not used when the anchor is a company.

include.description:
'LINK_INFO' adds a description and supporting evidence per connection (use when the
user wants to know WHY a connection exists). 'COMPANY_INFO' adds the company's own
profile. Omit both for a compact list of bare connections.

max.description:
Maximum number of connections to return per group. Small to stay focused, larger to
enumerate more fully.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 10.

name: get_company_themes
title: Get Company Themes
description:
Given a company, return the sectors, trends, and industries it belongs to, and for each one the top peer companies ranked by relevance.
Use for questions like 'what sectors is NVIDIA in?', 'what trends is Tesla part of?', or 'who are Apple's closest peers?' Requires the company's contract_id.
If you only have a name or ticker, call search_contracts first to resolve it.
Choose this over get_company_connections when you only need sectors/trends + ranked peers.
If you need the company's products, countries, regions, broader competitor view, or evidence text explaining each link, use get_company_connections instead.

contract_id.description:
Contract ID of the company, from search_contracts or get_theme_details. Resolve via
search_contracts if you only have a name or ticker.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 265598.

max_themes.description: Number of top themes to return for the company. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 5.

max_companies.description: Number of peer companies to return per theme, ranked by thematic relevance. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 5.

name: get_theme_details
title: Get Theme Details
description:
Return the full profile of an investment topic: its description, the companies in it ranked by relevance (rank 1 = most central — this is relevance-ranked, NOT market-cap-weighted), and optionally ETFs/mutual funds with exposure.
Use after search_investment_topics when the user wants to know which companies are in a sector or trend ('which companies are in AI?', 'top battery stocks', 'what ETFs cover clean energy').
Requires a key obtained verbatim from search_investment_topics.
Each returned company includes a contract_id that can be passed directly into get_company_themes or get_company_connections to go deeper.
For large topics, use offset together with the returned total_count to paginate through the full company list.

key.description:
Theme key returned verbatim by search_investment_topics. Do not construct or guess — must come
from a prior search_investment_topics result.

max.description: Max companies to return, in rank order. Combine with offset to paginate. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 20.

offset.description:
Starting index into the rank-ordered company list, for pagination. To page through a
large theme, increment offset by max each call and stop when offset reaches the
returned total_count.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 20.

max_funds.description:
Number of ETFs/mutual funds with exposure to include. Defaults to 0 (no funds).
Set greater than 0 only when the user asks about funds or ETFs.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 20.

name: search_investment_topics
title: Search Investment Topics
description:
Search for companies grouped by sector, industry, trend, or topic.
Use when the user asks about an investment area ('who's in solar', 'AI stocks', 'clean energy companies', 'what's happening in quantum computing').
Returns matching topics as {key, name} pairs.
Pass the returned key to get_theme_details for the full company list.
Query tips: use short, broad, singular keywords — a single root noun ('battery', not 'batteries' or 'electric vehicle batteries'; 'robot', not 'robotics companies').
The matcher is keyword-based and narrow, so plural or multi-word queries often return nothing.
If results are empty, retry with a shorter/singular form or a synonym before concluding no match exists.
Never guess, construct, or modify a key — only pass keys returned by this tool.

query.description:
Short, broad keyword for the topic or sector, ideally a single singular noun (e.g.
'battery', 'lithium', 'quantum', 'solar'). Avoid plurals and multi-word phrases,
which frequently return no matches; retry with a shorter or singular variant if empty.

name: get_price_history
title: Get Price History
description:
Returns historical OHLCV (open/high/low/close/volume) price bars for an instrument over a specified time period.
Use when the user asks about price trends, historical performance, or wants to compare prices across dates.
Provide either period or step_count but never both.
When called with an option contract_id from get_option_data, use security_type="OPT" and pass the exchange field from that row; if no exchange is available, omit it to default to SMART.

contract_id.description: Contract identifier for the instrument. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 265598.

exchange.description: Contract exchange. Omit to use SMART (aggregated best execution).

security_type.description:
Security type of the contract:
STK (stocks),
OPT (options),
FUT (futures),
FOP (futures options),
CASH (cash),
WAR (warrants),
BOND (bonds),
CFD (contracts for difference),
FUND (mutual funds),
IND (indices),
CRYPTO (cryptocurrency),
CMDTY (commodities),
IOPT (issuer options).
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

period.description:
Time period. Required when step_count is not provided; mutually exclusive with step_count (never provide both).
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

step.description:
Bar size.
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

step_count.description:
Number of bars to return. Required when period is not provided; mutually exclusive with period (never provide both).
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 30.

outside_rth.description: Include data outside regular trading hours (RTH). Pass as a JSON boolean (true/false), not the string "true"/"false".

include_corporate_actions.description: When set to true, response will include corporate actions for the specified chart period. Pass as a JSON boolean (true/false), not the string "true"/"false".

name: get_price_snapshot
title: Get Price Snapshot
description:
Retrieves a real-time market data snapshot for an instrument.
Allows requesting one or more market data fields in a single call.
Use this to get the current price, bid/ask spread, volume, volatility, and other live market metrics.
For historical OHLCV price bars use get_price_history instead.
Note on response key casing: response JSON keys use hyphens where requested field names use underscores.
For example, requesting `option_midpoint_iv` returns the key `option-midpoint-iv` in the response; `bid_ask` → `bid-ask`; `option_open_interest` → `option-open-interest`.
Always look up response values using the hyphenated form, not the underscore form used in market_data_names.
Note: SMART routing only covers SMART-eligible instruments (US equities and equity options).
For futures and futures options, pass the contract's native `exchange` (from search_futures / get_option_parameters / search_contracts) or the response will be empty.

contract_id.description:
Contract identifier for the instrument.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 265598.

exchange.description:
Exchange of the instrument.
For SMART-eligible instruments (US stocks, ETFs, and equity options), this is optional — if omitted, SMART routing is used.
For instruments NOT eligible for SMART routing — notably futures (FUT) and futures options (FOP) — omitting this returns NO market data; you MUST pass the contract's native exchange (e.g. CME for ES/NQ, CBOT, NYMEX, COMEX, EUREX).
The correct value is the `exchange` field on the contract row returned by search_futures, get_option_data, or search_contracts — pass it verbatim.
When the contract came from search_futures or is a FOP, always set this.

market_data_names.description:
Optional list of market data fields to request.
 If omitted, a default set of ['last', 'bid_ask'] is used.
 Provide specific fields only when you need more than the basic quote.
 Supported market data names (values for the 'market_data_names' input field):
  - bid_ask: Current bid and ask prices for the instrument.
  - last: Last trade price with timestamp and halt/close status flags. Price can be null if a trade happened at the same price as the previous one (only timestamp field (ts) changes).
  - top_status: Market data status for top subscription (REALTIME, DELAYED, FROZEN, FROZEN_DELAYED, REJECT)
  - change: Absolute price change and percentage change from the prior session close.
  - prior_close: Prior session closing price.
  - plprice: Mark price (profit/loss price). Also called the as-known-as mark-price.
  - dividend_yield: Dividend yield percentage for STK and CFD instruments. Rounded to 1 decimal place.
  - volume: Today's total trading volume for the instrument.
  - option_volume: Option trading volume for today for individual option contracts (OPT and FOP).
  - option_open_interest: Option put and call open interest for individual option contracts (OPT and FOP).
  - future_open_interest: Open interest for futures (FUT) contracts.
  - option_midpoint_iv: Midpoint implied volatility for individual option contracts (OPT and FOP).
  - option_greeks: Option Greeks and theoretical option price for individual option contracts (OPT and FOP).
    Returns an object with delta, gamma, theta, vega, and option_price.
  - underlying_today_option_volume: Total today's option put/call volume for the underlying.
  - underlying_avg_option_volume: Average option put/call volume for the underlying.
  - misc_statistics: Historical 13-week, 26-week, and 52-week high and low prices, plus open price 52 weeks ago.
  - avg_90d_usd_volume: Average USD trading volume over the last 90 calendar days.
  - implied_volatility_percentile: Implied volatility high percentile over 13-week, 26-week, and
    52-week windows. Values are fractions (e.g. 0.94 = 94th percentile).
  - implied_vol_underlying: Implied volatility for the underlying. Values are fractions
  (multiply by 100 to get percentage). Usually the annual_iv is displayed to clients.
  - implied_vol: Implied volatility for option contracts. Values are fractions.
  - historical_vol: Historical volatility for the last 30 days. Values are fractions.
  - year_to_date_change: Year-to-date price change from last year's close. Available for STK and indices.
  - bond_yield: Bid yield and ask yield (yield-to-worst) for BOND instruments only.
  - cumulative_perf_1d: 1-day cumulative performance percentage for ETFs, mutual funds, or stocks.
  - cumulative_perf_1w: 1-week cumulative performance percentage.
  - cumulative_perf_1m: 1-month cumulative performance percentage.
  - cumulative_perf_ytd: Year-to-date cumulative performance percentage.
  - cumulative_perf_1y: 1-year cumulative performance percentage.
  - cumulative_perf_3y: 3-year cumulative performance percentage.
  - cumulative_perf_5y: 5-year cumulative performance percentage.
  - total_net_assets: Total net assets value for ETFs, mutual funds, or stocks.
  - open: Today's market open price.
  - low: Today's intraday lowest price.
  - high: Today's intraday highest price.
  - perpetual_futures_funding_rate: Perpetual crypto futures funding rate and next funding time.
Notes:
 - Multiple fields can be requested in a single call.
 - Clients receive realtime or delayed prices automatically based on their market data subscription.
 - Fields that are unavailable or time out within 10 seconds are omitted from the response besides bid and ask which may return as an empty object when no quote is currently available for the instrument.

name: create_order_instruction
title: Create Order Instruction
description:
Creates a new instruction. An instruction is not a live order. Requires
flow_type=REVIEW_AND_APPROVE. In AUTONOMOUS flow, use submit_order instead, which submits
a live order directly rather than a reviewable instruction.
The returned URL deep-links to the instruction in the IBKR platforms where a user can review and submit it. Always surface this url to the user — it is required for them to review and submit the instruction, and no other tool exposes it.
quantity, order_type, limit_price, and time_in_force are all optional; any left
unset can be filled in by the user when reviewing the instruction at the
deep-link URL before submission. Only side is strictly required beyond the
contract identifier.
After submission, the instruction is converted into a live order.
Supports Stocks (STK), Futures (FUT), single-leg Options (OPT), single-leg
Futures Options (FOP), and OPT–OPT option combos/spreads. Combo/spread support
is limited to equity-option (OPT) legs only; FOP, FUT, STK, and mixed-type
combos are not supported.

contract_id_ex.description:
Full contract identifier.
For STK: stringify the underlying_contract_id from search_contracts (e.g. "8314").
For FUT: use contract_id_ex from search_futures verbatim (e.g. "12345@CME").
For OPT/FOP: use call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "722271932@CBOE").
For combos/spreads: use contract_id_ex from get_combo_identifier verbatim.
Optional only when the deprecated contract_id parameter is supplied.
Always a JSON string, even when it looks numeric — e.g. "8314", never the number 8314.

contract_id.description:
Deprecated — use contract_id_ex instead.
Numeric contract identifier from search_contracts (underlying_contract_id), search_futures (contract_id), or get_option_data (call_contract_id / put_contract_id).
Accepted as a backward-compatibility fallback; contract_id_ex takes precedence when both are supplied.
Supply exactly one of contract_id_ex or contract_id.
Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 530965695.

side.description: Side: BUY or SELL. Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

quantity.description: Number of units (shares for STK; contracts for FUT, OPT, and FOP). The same concept as submit_order's size / modify_order's quantity, under yet another parameter name. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 15, not "15".

order_type.description: Order type: MARKET or LIMIT. Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

limit_price.description: Limit price. Required when order_type is LIMIT; ignored otherwise. Pass as a JSON number, unquoted — e.g. 198.5.

time_in_force.description:
Specifies how long the order remains active before it expires.
Allowed values:
DAY (Day Order - valid only for the current trading day, cancelled if not filled by session end),
GTC (Good Till Cancelled - remains active until fully executed or explicitly cancelled),
OVT (Overnight - executed during the overnight trading session after regular market close),
OND (Overnight Next Day - placed for the overnight session, carries over into the next trading day if unfilled),
OPG (At The Opening - executed at the market opening auction on the next trading day).
There is no outside_rth flag here — OVT/OND already encode the extended-session
behavior directly.
If not provided, the system default time-in-force policy is applied.
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

name: delete_order_instruction
title: Delete Order Instruction
description: Deletes an existing instruction by its ID. Requires flow_type=REVIEW_AND_APPROVE. In AUTONOMOUS flow, use cancel_order instead to cancel a live order.

id.description: ID of the order instruction to delete. Pass as a JSON string, quoted — e.g. "124", not the number 124. Copy verbatim from the id field returned by get_order_instructions.

name: get_order_instructions
title: Get Order Instructions
description:
Returns all saved instructions for the account. Not flow-restricted — usable
under either flow_type.
Each instruction includes an ID, description, contract identifier (contract_id_ex), trade direction (BUY/SELL), quantity, order type (MARKET/LIMIT), limit price, time in force, creation time (ISO 8601), and expiration (ISO 8601, if present).

name: answer_order_question
title: Answer Order Question
description:
Sends an answer to a broker confirmation raised by submit_order, modify_order, or
cancel_order. A confirming answer on the final question releases that action to the
market (placing, modifying, or cancelling the order); a declining answer voids it.
Only confirm placement or modification of STK or single-leg OPT orders; decline
questions for unsupported security types. Cancellation may still be confirmed.
Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow never produces a pending_question,
since instructions are not live orders — there is nothing to answer under REVIEW_AND_APPROVE
flow.
PRECONDITIONS: a non-null pending_question in a submit_order, modify_order,
cancel_order, or prior answer_order_question result. See submit_order for the full
sequence.
RESULT: same shape as submit_order. An answer may produce another pending_question
instead of an outcome; handle it the same way. The action is settled only when a
result has no pending_question: until then no order exists on the market (for
submit_order), or the modification or cancellation has not been applied (for
modify_order and cancel_order). That result carries the order_id and order_status
of the outcome.
RULES:
- correlation_id must be the value from the result that produced this
pending_question — copy it verbatim; it is echoed back in this result so it can be
carried into the next round.
PENDING QUESTIONS:
- The broker may return several pending_questions in sequence. Evaluate each question
separately and call answer_order_question with an answer value copied verbatim from
pending_question.answers and this result's correlation_id, until a result has no
pending_question.
- If the user has explicitly given you permission to answer broker questions on their
behalf, you may answer automatically within that permission and the user's stated
instructions and limits. Do not ask the user again for questions covered by that
permission. Permission to place, modify, or cancel an order, or flow_type=AUTONOMOUS,
does not by itself grant permission to answer broker questions.
- Without that permission, or if a question is outside its scope, the appropriate
answer is unclear, or answering would conflict with the user's instructions or limits,
present the question to the user and obtain their answer before calling
answer_order_question. Honor any withdrawal of permission for subsequent questions.
- Do not blindly confirm every question or choose an answer just because it is marked
default. User permission does not override the supported security types or other tool
rules.
- No order exists on the market until the final question is answered with a confirming
value and a result returns an order_id. Modification or cancellation is not applied
until its final question is answered with a confirming value.
ON ERROR: the question expires about 2 minutes after it was raised, cancelling the
underlying action; answering an expired question returns an error saying so — then
call get_order_status (or get_account_orders with show_completed=true if there is
no order_id yet) to confirm the outcome rather than retrying, and report it. For any
other error or timeout, do not retry; escalate to the user.

question_id.description: question_id being answered. Globally unique across all of the user's orders — you don't need order_id to know which order a question belongs to.

value.description: Answer value, copied verbatim from an entry in pending_question.answers.

correlation_id.description: The correlation_id from the submit_order, modify_order, cancel_order, or answer_order_question result that produced this pending_question. Copy it verbatim and unchanged; it correlates this answer with the request it belongs to.

name: cancel_order
title: Cancel Order
description:
Requests cancellation of a LIVE working order identified by order_id, with real
money; fills that happen before the cancellation is processed are irreversible.
Agentic Trading only places STK and single-leg OPT orders; cancellation of an
existing order is still permitted to reduce exposure.
Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. In REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow, use delete_order_instruction
instead to remove an instruction before it is submitted.
PRECONDITIONS: the order's order_id. See submit_order for the full sequence.
RESULT: same shape as submit_order. Cancellation is a request, not a guarantee —
the exchange may fill the order before the cancellation is processed. Do not assume
order_status is CANCELLED; report the actual outcome, including filled_quantity. The
cancellation is not applied until any pending_question is answered with a confirming
value.
RULES: cancel_order is idempotent — cancelling an order that is already cancelled
returns the same outcome rather than an error — and it can be called on an order
with an outstanding modify_order question, voiding that question.
PENDING QUESTIONS: if pending_question is non-null, follow the pending-question policy
in submit_order and pass this result's correlation_id to answer_order_question.
ON ERROR: if this call returns an error or times out, do not call it again: the broker
may already have accepted the request. Look for the order's order_id in
get_account_orders — pass show_completed=true, since the order may have already
completed — and confirm it with get_order_status; for fill price and commission, call
get_account_trades (symbol, side, size, trade_time). Then escalate with what you found.

order_id.description: order_id returned by submit_order, modify_order, cancel_order, answer_order_question, get_order_status, or get_account_orders.

name: get_order_rules
title: Get Order Rules
description:
Returns the order types and times in force permitted for a contract and side under
autonomous order submission. Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow has no
order-rules tool — order type constraints are enforced when the instruction is
reviewed and submitted.
Only use these rules for STK and single-leg OPT contracts. Rules returned for
FUT, FOP, combos/spreads, or other security types do not authorize live placement
through Agentic Trading.
PRECONDITIONS: pass is_position_close when the order closes a position, and
order_id when checking a modification of an existing order, since both change the
permitted set. See submit_order for the full sequence.
RESULT:
- order_types: per-entry capability objects, not a flat allow-list. Each entry
reports outside_rth and cash_quantity (whether cash_size may be used) for that
order_type. A flag may be absent; treat an absent flag as false — e.g. absent
cash_quantity means cash_size is not allowed.
- tifs: each entry reports outside_rth and the order_types it can be combined with.
RULES:
- Only values present both here AND in the submit_order/modify_order order_type and
tif enums are usable; these lists describe everything the broker supports for the
contract and may include values those tools do not accept.
- Check the specific flags for the requested order_type/tif, not just presence in
the list.
- If the instruction requires an order_type, tif, size kind, or price outside these
capabilities, do not substitute a different value: escalate to the user with
the mismatch and the supported alternatives from this result.
- is_position_close: set to true only when the order reduces an existing position;
buying more of an instrument already held long is false.
ON ERROR: do not retry; escalate to the user.

contract_id_ex.description:
Full contract identifier.
For STK: stringify the underlying_contract_id from search_contracts (e.g. "8314").
For OPT: use call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from an OPT option chain
returned by get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "722271932@CBOE").
Agentic Trading orders support only STK and single-leg OPT. Do not use FUT,
FOP, combos/spreads, or any other security type, even if its contract_id_ex
is available from another tool.
Always a JSON string, even when it looks numeric — e.g. "8314", never the number 8314.

side.description: Side: BUY or SELL. Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

is_position_close.description:
Set to true only when this order reduces an existing position (closing all or part of
it). Buying more of an instrument already held long is false; pass false for any order
that opens or increases a position.

order_id.description: order_id of the working order being modified, as returned by submit_order, modify_order, get_order_status, or get_account_orders; omit for a new order.

name: get_order_status
title: Get Order Status
description:
Retrieves the current status and parameters of an order identified by order_id.
Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. In REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow, use
get_account_orders to check the status of an order instead.
PRECONDITIONS: an order_id from submit_order, modify_order, cancel_order,
answer_order_question, or a prior get_order_status call. See submit_order for the
full sequence.
RESULT:
- order_status: one of CANCELLED, DONE_FOR_THE_DAY, EXPIRED, FILLED, NEW,
PARTIALLY_FILLED, PENDING_CANCEL, PENDING_CANCEL_REPLACE, PENDING_NEW,
PENDING_REPLACE, REJECTED, or REPLACED.
- total_quantity, filled_quantity, remaining_quantity: order size, filled part, and
unfilled part, in the instrument's units.
- contract_id_ex, side, order_type, tif, limit_price, stop_price, outside_rth: the
order's current parameters — use them as the baseline before calling modify_order.
Only modify STK or single-leg OPT orders in Agentic Trading. A status result for
another security type does not make that order eligible for modification.
limit_price and stop_price may be 0 when they do not apply to the order_type (e.g.
MARKET); ignore them for those order types and never report them as prices.
- No fill price or actual commission. For the final report, call
get_account_trades, which returns each execution's price and commission; match by
symbol, side, size, and trade_time.
- Outstanding questions are never reported here — only by the submit_order,
modify_order, cancel_order, or answer_order_question call that raised them.
RULES:
- DONE_FOR_THE_DAY and EXPIRED may include partial fills. Always report
filled_quantity and remaining_quantity.

order_id.description: order_id returned by submit_order, modify_order, cancel_order, answer_order_question, a prior get_order_status call, or get_account_orders.

name: modify_order
title: Modify Order
description:
Modifies a LIVE working order identified by order_id, with real money; fills,
including fills at the new parameters, are irreversible. Requires
flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow has no order-modification tool — delete the
instruction with delete_order_instruction and recreate it with
create_order_instruction instead.
Only modify STK or single-leg OPT orders. Do not modify FUT, FOP,
combos/spreads, or any other security type through Agentic Trading.
Replaces the order's parameters in full, mirroring submit_order — there is no
partial/delta update. Every field is required on every call; fields you are not
changing must still be passed with their current value (the baseline from
get_order_status).
PRECONDITIONS — the canonical sequence for every order modification, mirroring
submit_order:
(1) get_flow_type returns AUTONOMOUS.
(2) get_order_status for the order's current contract_id_ex, side, order_type, tif,
size, and prices, to use as the baseline for any field you are not changing.
(3) Call get_order_rules with contract_id_ex, side, and order_id. Check order_type,
tif, size kind.
(4) Call preview_order with the exact final parameters — the complete new state of
the order, not just the fields that changed.
(5) Self-verify the preview: errors is absent or empty; instrument, side, size,
order_type, tif, and prices match the user's instruction; cost, size, and position
change are within any limits the user stated. If any check fails, escalate to the user.
(6) Call modify_order with byte-identical parameters, in the same turn.
(7) Handle pending_question per PENDING QUESTIONS in submit_order.
RESULT: same shape as submit_order. The same order_id continues to identify the
order after modification — modify_order does not mint a new order_id. The
modification is not applied until any pending_question is answered with a
confirming value; afterwards report the new parameters.
PENDING QUESTIONS: if pending_question is non-null, follow the pending-question policy
in submit_order and pass this result's correlation_id to answer_order_question.
ON ERROR: if this call returns an error or times out, do not call it again: the broker
may already have accepted the request. Look for the order's order_id in
get_account_orders — pass show_completed=true, since the order may have already
completed — and confirm it with get_order_status; for fill price and commission, call
get_account_trades (symbol, side, size, trade_time). Then escalate with what you found.

order_id.description: order_id returned by submit_order, modify_order, cancel_order, answer_order_question, get_order_status, or get_account_orders.

contract_id_ex.description: The order's current contract_id_ex, exactly as returned by get_order_status.

side.description: The order's current side, exactly as returned by get_order_status — modify_order cannot change an order's side.

order_type.description:
Order type.
MARKET - executes immediately at the best available price.
LIMIT - executes at limit_price or better.
STOP - becomes a market order once stop_price is reached.
STOP_LIMIT - becomes a limit order at limit_price once stop_price is reached.
Must also appear in get_order_rules' order_types for this contract.
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

tif.description:
Time in force.
DAY - valid only for the current trading session; cancelled if unfilled by session end.
OVT (Overnight) - executed during the overnight trading session after regular market close.
OND (Overnight Next Day) - placed for the overnight session, carries over into the next trading day if unfilled.
Must also appear in get_order_rules' tifs for this contract, with order_type in that entry's order_types.
outside_rth only applies when tif is DAY — OVT and OND already encode the extended-session behavior directly.
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

size.description:
Order size in the instrument's units: shares for STK; contracts for OPT.
If the user says "shares" for an OPT order, treat that as contracts and use
the correct unit in reports. Must be a whole number — fractional share quantities are
not allowed in Agentic Trading. Decimal limit_price and stop_price are allowed. New order size — an absolute new value, not a delta and not additive to the existing size. Supply exactly one of size or cash_size.

cash_size.description:
New order size in cash terms, denominated in the contract's trading currency (not the
account's base currency) — an absolute new value, not a delta and not additive to the
existing cash size. Valid for STK only, and only when get_order_rules reports
cash_quantity=true for the order_type. Supply exactly one of size or cash_size.

limit_price.description: Limit price. Required when order_type is LIMIT or STOP_LIMIT; ignored otherwise.

stop_price.description: Stop (trigger) price. Required when order_type is STOP or STOP_LIMIT; ignored otherwise.

outside_rth.description: Allow execution outside regular trading hours during the current session. Only applies when tif is DAY — OVT and OND already specify the overnight session directly and ignore this flag.

is_position_close.description:
Set to true only when this order reduces an existing position (closing all or part of
it). Buying more of an instrument already held long is false; pass false for any order
that opens or increases a position.

name: preview_order
title: Preview Order
description:
Computes the estimated cost, commission, and position/equity/margin impact of an
order without submitting it. Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow has no
order-preview tool — call create_order_instruction to create a reviewable
instruction instead.
Only preview STK and single-leg OPT orders for Agentic Trading. Do not preview
FUT, FOP, combos/spreads, or any other security type for live placement.
PRECONDITIONS: get_order_rules has confirmed the parameters are supported. Pass the
exact final parameters you intend to submit. See submit_order for the full sequence
and the self-verification step.
RESULT:
- amount: estimated trade value, excluding commission;
- commission: estimated commission;
- total: amount + commission;
- position.current/change/after: position size in the instrument's units (shares
or contracts).
- funds.current/change/after: account equity before the order, the change, and
after. This is equity, not cash or available funds, so it does not show cash
spent — use total for that.
- initial_margin, maintenance_margin: current/change/after.
- funds and margin values may carry no currency suffix; do not attach a currency
to them in reports unless one is shown.
- warnings: list of {suppress_id, text}. Warnings do not block submission, but
include each warning's text, exactly as written, in the final report.
- errors: list of {text}. Absent or empty means no errors. Non-empty means the
broker would reject the order: do not call submit_order; escalate to the user.
RULES:
- Verify the preview yourself (submit_order step 6), then call submit_order in the
same turn with byte-identical parameters.
- If you change any parameter after previewing, preview again before submitting.
- Preview does NOT surface the confirmation questions submit_order may raise. A
passing preview does not mean submission needs no further answers.
ON ERROR: preview never places an order. Do not retry; escalate to the user.

contract_id_ex.description:
Full contract identifier.
For STK: stringify the underlying_contract_id from search_contracts (e.g. "8314").
For OPT: use call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from an OPT option chain
returned by get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "722271932@CBOE").
Agentic Trading orders support only STK and single-leg OPT. Do not use FUT,
FOP, combos/spreads, or any other security type, even if its contract_id_ex

name: submit_order
title: Submit Order
description:
Submits a LIVE order with real money in the user's account; fills are irreversible. Requires flow_type=AUTONOMOUS. In REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow, use create_order_instruction instead, which creates a reviewable instruction rather than a live order. Only STK (stocks) and single-leg OPT (equity/index options) orders are supported in Agentic Trading. Do not submit FUT, FOP, combos/spreads, or any other security type; if the user requests one, explain that live placement is unavailable. PRECONDITIONS — the canonical sequence for every order: (1) get_flow_type returns AUTONOMOUS. (2) Resolve contract_id_ex: search_contracts for STK, get_option_data for a single-leg OPT from an OPT option chain. Do not use a FOP option chain. (3) Call get_order_rules with contract_id_ex, side, and is_position_close. Check order_type, tif, size kind (size or cash_size). (4) Call preview_order with the exact final parameters. (5) Self-verify the preview: errors is absent or empty; instrument, side, size, order_type, tif, and prices match the user's instruction; cost, size, and position change are within any limits the user stated. If any check fails, escalate to the user. (6) Call submit_order with byte-identical parameters, in the same turn. (7) Handle pending_question per PENDING QUESTIONS below. PENDING QUESTIONS: - The broker may return several pending_questions in sequence. Evaluate each question separately and call answer_order_question with an answer value copied verbatim from pending_question.answers and this result's correlation_id, until a result has no pending_question. - If the user has explicitly given you permission to answer broker questions on their behalf, you may answer automatically within that permission and the user's stated instructions and limits. Do not ask the user again for questions covered by that permission. Permission to place, modify, or cancel an order, or flow_type=AUTONOMOUS, does not by itself grant permission to answer broker questions. - Without that permission, or if a question is outside its scope, the appropriate answer is unclear, or answering would conflict with the user's instructions or limits, present the question to the user and obtain their answer before calling answer_order_question. Honor any withdrawal of permission for subsequent questions. - Do not blindly confirm every question or choose an answer just because it is marked default. User permission does not override the supported security types or other tool rules. - No order exists on the market until the final question is answered with a confirming value and a result returns an order_id. Modification or cancellation is not applied until its final question is answered with a confirming value. ESCALATION — stop and involve the user only when: - preview_order returns non-empty errors; - get_order_rules does not support the order_type, tif, size kind, or price the instruction requires (do not silently substitute a different value); - a pending_question requires the user's answer under the pending-question policy; - the preview does not match the user's instruction (instrument, side, size, order_type, price) or exceeds any limits the user stated; - an order ends REJECTED; - any call errors or times out (see ON ERROR). When escalating: - Present broker messages (pending_question.message, errors, reject_reason) with their wording exactly as written, converting markup such as ,
, to the client's formatting (for example markdown), preserving all links, and dropping HTML entities like  . Never paraphrase, summarize, or omit sentences. - If the user asks what a broker message means, do not invent an explanation. Say the broker gave no further detail, and share any link in the message. - A pending_question expires about 2 minutes after it was raised, so tell the user. If it expires, the action is cancelled. REPORT, once a result has no pending_question: - instrument, side, size (with units), order_type, tif; - order_status, filled_quantity, remaining_quantity; - any preview warnings, with their text exactly as written; - every broker question that was answered, with its message text shown exactly as the broker wrote it and the answer given. ON ERROR: if this call returns an error or times out, do not call it again: the broker may already have accepted the request. Look for the order's order_id in get_account_orders — pass show_completed=true, since the order may have already completed — and confirm it with get_order_status; for fill price and commission, call get_account_trades (symbol, side, size, trade_time). Then escalate with what you found.

name: get_account_orders
title: Get Account Orders
description:
Retrieves the list of orders for the user. Not flow-restricted — usable under either
flow_type.
Each order includes order_id, symbol, side, order type, status, quantity, price, and fill information. In AUTONOMOUS flow, order_id can be used with get_order_status, modify_order, and cancel_order; those tools are unavailable in REVIEW_AND_APPROVE flow.
By default only working (not yet completed) orders are returned. Pass show_completed=true
to also include orders that completed today (filled, cancelled, etc.), which can reduce
the need for separate get_account_trades calls when reporting on recent fills.

show_completed.description: Include orders that completed today (filled, cancelled, etc.) in addition to working orders. Defaults to false (working orders only).

name: get_pa_allocation
title: Portfolio Allocation
description:
Returns the portfolio's NAV broken down along one category dimension into long and (when present) short buckets, each with a `total` and an `items` list carrying id, name, nav, and weight.
`short_positions` is only present when the account holds shorts in that dimension — consumers must null-check it.
Weights sum to 1.0 within each bucket independently.
The long-side total denominator is category-dependent (netted of shorts for ASSET_CLASS and FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT, gross for SECTOR/REGION/COUNTRY), so do not assume a common base across type values.
Item `id` codes are opaque internal keys — display `name`, never interpret id.
Related tools: get_account_positions, get_account_balances, search_contracts.

type.description:
The breakdown dimension: FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT, ASSET_CLASS, SECTOR, REGION, or COUNTRY.
ALL returns every dimension in a single response — prefer it over five separate calls for a full picture.
Case-sensitive: use the uppercase value exactly as listed.

currency.description:
Three-letter currency code; default USD (account base currency).
Requesting any non-base currency silently switches the response to the prior trading day with realtime:false — it does NOT return live data.
Verify FX conversion is applied before relying on the figures.

date.description:
Historical snapshot date in yyyymmdd; omit for the live current-day view.
Returns realtime:false with the date echoed.
Must be on or after account inception (the `start` field from get_pa_performance_all_periods); earlier dates return a generic, non-retryable server error.
Pass as a JSON string, quoted — e.g. "20260630", not the number 20260630.

name: get_pa_performance_all_periods
title: Portfolio Performance - All Periods
description:
Returns the account's performance time series for every available window (1D, 7D, MTD, 1M, YTD, 1Y).
Within each period, `cps`, `nav`, and `dates` are parallel arrays of equal length indexed together.
`cps` values are cumulative returns expressed as fractions measured from the period start (e.g. -0.106 = -10.6%), not percentages.
The return method is reported in the top-level `portfolio_measure` field as TWR (time-weighted) or MWR (money-weighted), set by account configuration.
For accounts younger than one year the 1Y series equals YTD, and inception-keyed periods may report start_nav 0.0 while the first element of the `nav` array holds the true opening value.
Related tools: get_account_positions, get_account_trades, get_price_history (for benchmarking the nav series).

Retrieves cash balances and market values broken down by currency.
Returns one entry per currency.

name: get_account_positions

description:
Retrieves all open positions.
Each position includes quantity, price, market value, P&L, and cost basis.

name: get_account_summary

description:
Retrieves account-level financial metrics:
net liquidation value, equity with loan value, available funds, buying power, initial and maintenance margin, day trading status, and alike.

name: create_saved_screener
title: Create Saved Screener
description:
Creates a saved screener definition. The definition contains its name, asset-class
selector, exchange location IDs, sorting scanner (sort code), filters, and factors.
Choose the selector from get_screener_asset_classes if it is not already known.
Check get_screener_templates for the selected selector when creating a new screener.
If a template clearly matches the user's request, use its filters and scanner or factors
as a starting point, adapting them to the requested criteria. If none fits, build the
definition from capabilities; a template is not required.
Before creating, call get_screener_capabilities exactly once for the selected selector
and use its returned IDs and codes for criteria you add or change. For industry or
investment-theme filtering, call get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes and include the selected exact
{code, value, label} object in filters. Factors use the
{id, weight} format: weights +1 through +3 prioritize higher values, while -1 through
-3 prioritize lower values; an absolute weight of 3 is most important. A screener may
contain both a sorting scanner and factors: any non-zero-weight factor takes precedence, while
the sorting scanner determines the result order when factors are absent or all weights are
zero. Provide a sorting scanner or at least one non-zero-weight factor. The screener name must
be no more than 40 characters. MultiSort allows at most 10 sort factors; if more are
requested, ask the user which 10 to keep. Before saving, use preview_screener to test
the configuration. Saving validates the definition before it is created. If the name is
already used, a numeric suffix is added. Returns id, content hash, and saved name.

name.description: Display name for the screener; maximum 40 characters. A numeric suffix is added if the name is taken.

selector.description: Required asset-class selector from get_screener_asset_classes or a known supported selector; verify its criteria with get_screener_capabilities.

locations.description: At least one exchange location ID, valid for the chosen asset-class selector and returned by get_screener_capabilities.

scanner.description: Sorting scanner: pass a scanners[].code returned by get_screener_capabilities. Used when factors are absent or all weights are zero; retained but ignored when any factor has a non-zero weight.

filters.description: Optional complete list of filters: [{code, value, label}]. Use label for industryLike and stockThemeIs filters returned by get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes; it is optional for ordinary filters. Defaults to [].

factors.description: Complete list of at most 10 MultiSort factors in {id, weight} format, including zero-weight factors. Use IDs returned by get_screener_capabilities. Weights +1 through +3 prioritize higher values, while -1 through -3 prioritize lower values. Any non-zero weight activates factor-based ranking and takes precedence over scanner; zero-weight factors do not activate factor ranking.

name: delete_saved_screener
title: Delete Saved Screener
description: Permanently deletes a saved screener identified by screener_id. This action is irreversible. The ID must come from list_saved_screeners. Confirm with the user before calling.

screener_id.description: Saved screener identifier returned by list_saved_screeners.

name: get_saved_screener
title: Get Saved Screener
description:
Returns the full definition of a saved screener for inspection or reuse. This
describes its criteria, not its current results; use run_saved_screener to retrieve
matching instruments. When presenting a definition with one or more non-zero-weight
factors, describe the factor ranking and do not describe the scanner; the scanner is
returned only so the complete saved definition can be preserved on update.
The details object contains:
name (string): display name.
selector (string): asset-class selector used by this saved definition. Use
get_screener_asset_classes to resolve its product and region when needed.
locations (array of strings): exchange location IDs included in this saved definition;
get_screener_capabilities lists valid locations for its selector.
scanner (string, optional): sorting scanner (sort code) returned by
get_screener_capabilities. Sort codes commonly follow SCAN_<metric>_<ASC|DESC>, where
ASC ranks lower values first and DESC ranks higher values first; for example,
SCAN_changePerc_ASC ranks the largest percentage decliners first and
SCAN_changePerc_DESC ranks the largest percentage gainers first. Do not infer a code's
name or direction from this pattern: IMPVOLATCHANGEPERC uses
TOP_OPT_IMP_VOLAT_LOSE (decliners) and TOP_OPT_IMP_VOLAT_GAIN (gainers). This field is
returned as saved, including when it is ignored because the screener has one or more
non-zero-weight factors and uses factor-based ranking instead. Do not describe this
field when presenting a factor-ranked screener.
filters (array, optional): filter code and value pairs. Values are strings; codes and
units depend on the asset-class selector and exchange location. For example, avgVolumeAbove is measured
in shares and usdMarketCapAbove in US dollars.
factors (array, optional): factors use the {id, weight} format. Positive weights (+1
to +3) prioritize higher values; negative weights (-1 to -3) prioritize lower values;
an absolute weight of 3 is most important. Factors with a non-zero weight use
factor-based ranking; the returned sorting scanner is retained but does not apply. When factors are absent or all weights
are zero, the screener uses the sorting scanner to determine the result
order.

screener_id.description:
Saved screener id returned by list_saved_screeners. Pass it as a JSON string, for
example "2", not the number 2.

name: get_screener_asset_classes
title: Get Screener Asset Classes
description: Lists the supported screener asset-class selectors, their regions and products, and the default selection. Use the chosen selector with get_screener_capabilities.

name: get_screener_capabilities
title: Get Screener Capabilities
description:
Retrieves screener capabilities for exactly one asset-class selector: exchange
location IDs, aggregated criteria, and factor weights. Each criterion has a name
and may include a filter, scanners, and factor_id. Use a code from a criterion's
scanners to order results; each scanner includes its direction. Use factor_id for
factor sorting; factor_name is present only when different from the criterion name.
When present, the filter provides type, codes (above/below for range filters),
value_type, units, and histogram_id (an identifier, not histogram data). A
criterion can have a factor without a filter or scanners. Only range filters are
currently exposed; other filter types may have codes without above/below in the
future. Industries and investment themes are returned by the dedicated
get_screener_industries and get_screener_themes tools. Before calling, choose a
selector matching the user's requested product and region from
get_screener_asset_classes, or reuse a known supported selector. If the user has no
preference, use the selector marked as the default. Before creating, updating, or
configuring a screener for a selector, call this exactly once for that selector and use
only its returned IDs and codes. Capabilities are selector-specific; do not call this
again for the same selector during the same operation. The response is scoped to the
current authenticated user and requested selector.

selector.description:
Required asset-class selector. Match the requested product and region using
get_screener_asset_classes, or reuse a known supported selector.

name: get_screener_industries
title: Get Screener Industries
description:
Returns the industries supported by a selector, grouped by sector. Choose a selector
from get_screener_asset_classes if it is not already known. Call this when the
customer requests an industry filter; do not guess an industry value. Add the selected
industry to filters for preview_screener, create_saved_screener, or
update_saved_screener as {code: "industryLike", value: <industry value>, label:
<industry name>}. For example: {"code":"industryLike","value":"Basic
Materials|Mining","label":"Mining"}. The label makes the saved definition
understandable; the value must exactly match this tool's response. This filter can be
combined with ordinary capability filters and theme filters.

selector.description: Required asset-class selector; choose from get_screener_asset_classes or reuse a known supported selector.

name: get_screener_templates
title: Get Screener Templates
description: Retrieves ready-made screener templates for one asset-class selector. Choose a selector from get_screener_asset_classes if it is not already known. When a template clearly matches the customer's request, use its criteria as a starting point and adapt them to the requested filters and ranking; templates are optional. Templates provide filters and either a sorting scanner or ranking factors. Use get_screener_capabilities to verify codes you add or change.

selector.description: Required asset-class selector; choose from get_screener_asset_classes or reuse a known supported selector.

name: get_screener_themes
title: Get Screener Themes
description:
Returns the investment themes supported by a selector, grouped by theme group. Choose a
selector from get_screener_asset_classes if it is not already known. Call this
when the customer requests a theme filter; do not guess a theme value. Add the selected
theme to filters for preview_screener, create_saved_screener, or
update_saved_screener as {code: "stockThemeIs", value: <theme value>, label: <theme
name>}. For example: {"code":"stockThemeIs","value":"45","label":"Aviation
Safety"}. The label makes the saved definition understandable; the value must exactly
match this tool's response. This filter can be combined with ordinary capability filters
and industry filters.
