name: list_saved_screeners
title: List Saved Screeners
description:
Returns the user's saved screeners. Each entry contains:
id (string): screener identifier. Pass this value as a string to get_saved_screener or
run_saved_screener.
name (string): display name assigned to the screener.
hash (integer): content hash for the screener definition. Use it to detect
whether a cached definition is stale; it does not represent changes in its live
results.
Takes no parameters.

name: preview_screener
title: Preview Screener
description:
Validates a new screener configuration and runs it immediately. Choose the asset-class
selector from get_screener_asset_classes if it is not already known. Before running, call
get_screener_capabilities exactly once for this configuration's selector, then use only
its returned selector, location IDs, ordinary filter codes and value types,
scanner codes, and factor IDs and weights when building criteria from scratch or
adapting a template. For an industry or investment-theme request, also call
get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes and add the selected {code, value, label}
object to filters. If a clearly relevant template has already been found, use it as a
starting point and adapt its criteria to the user's request; otherwise build the criteria
from capabilities. A template is not required. This tool returns current matching
instruments; it does not save a screener. A screener may
contain both a sorting scanner and factors. Any
non-zero-weight factor activates factor-based ranking and takes precedence over the
sorting scanner. If factors are absent or all weights are zero, the sorting scanner determines the
result order. Provide a sorting scanner or at least one non-zero-weight factor. Factors use
{id, weight}: weights +1 through +3 prioritize higher values, while -1 through -3
prioritize lower values; an absolute weight of 3 is most important. MultiSort allows
at most 10 sort factors; if more are requested, ask the user which 10 to keep.

selector.description: Required asset-class selector from get_screener_asset_classes or a known supported selector; verify its criteria with get_screener_capabilities.

locations.description: At least one exchange location ID, valid for the chosen asset-class selector and returned by get_screener_capabilities.

filters.description: Optional complete list of filters: [{code, value, label}]. Use label for industryLike and stockThemeIs filters returned by get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes; it is optional for ordinary filters. Defaults to [].

scanner.description: Sorting scanner: pass a scanners[].code returned by get_screener_capabilities. Used when factors are absent or all weights are zero; retained but ignored when any factor has a non-zero weight.

factors.description: Complete list of at most 10 MultiSort factors in {id, weight} format, including zero-weight factors. Use IDs returned by get_screener_capabilities. Weights +1 through +3 prioritize higher values, while -1 through -3 prioritize lower values. Any non-zero weight activates factor-based ranking and takes precedence over scanner; zero-weight factors do not activate factor ranking.

max_results.description: Number of results from 1 to 50; defaults to 10.

name: run_saved_screener
title: Run Saved Screener
description:
Runs a saved screener and returns a current ranked snapshot of its matching
instruments.

If the user specified a screener name rather than an id, first resolve it with
list_saved_screeners. The response's definition field is the source of truth for the
parameters actually run. When presenting results, include the definition's name,
asset-class selector, exchange location IDs, and every filter with its units. For
screeners without active factors, include the sorting scanner (sort code) and explain its order in plain language (ASC =
lowest values first; DESC = highest values first). For screeners with one or more
non-zero-weight factors, describe the factor ranking instead and do not describe the
sorting scanner; it does not apply.
Unless the user gives explicit presentation instructions, display each result's rank,
contract_description, and company_name.

The response contains:

definition (object): the exact screener definition used for this run.
results (array): the matching instruments. Each result contains:

rank (integer): position in the screener's sort order, starting at 1.
contract_id (integer): IBKR contract identifier. Use this value with
get_price_snapshot or other contract-level tools to retrieve price, volume, and other
details.
company_name (string): human-readable company name of the instrument.
contract_description (string): human-readable name or description of the instrument.
score (number, factor screeners only): combined factor-ranking score.
factor_scores (array of numbers, factor screeners only): per-factor ranking scores,
in the same order as the screener's factors.

total_matched (integer): total number of instruments meeting the screener criteria.
url (string): direct link to open the screener in IBKR.

Results from a screener using a sorting scanner do not include the sort metric value,
price, or volume.

Results are a live snapshot: ranks, membership, and total_matched can change between
calls. The tool returns the first max_results results only, up to 50. It has no offset
or paging parameter, so positions beyond that limit cannot be retrieved. Definitions
with one or more non-zero-weight factors use factor-based ranking. Definitions with no
factors or only zero-weight factors use their scanner to determine result order. Both
modes return the same response shape.

screener_id.description:
Saved screener id returned by list_saved_screeners. Pass it as a JSON string, for
example "2", not the number 2.

max_results.description:
Number of results to return, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 10. Values outside this
range are rejected with an error.

name: update_saved_screener
title: Update Saved Screener
description:
Replaces the complete definition of an existing saved screener and returns its new
content hash and saved name. If the name is already used, a numeric suffix is added.
Preserve the selector from get_saved_screener unless changing asset class; for a new
selection, consult get_screener_asset_classes.
Before updating, call get_screener_capabilities exactly once for the
selected selector and use only its returned IDs and codes. For industry or
investment-theme filtering, call get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes and
include the selected exact {code, value, label} object in filters. Factors use the {id, weight} format: a positive weight
prioritizes higher values, a negative weight prioritizes lower values, and absolute
weights range from 1 (somewhat important) to 3 (most important). A screener may
contain both a sorting scanner and factors: any non-zero-weight factor takes precedence, while
the sorting scanner determines the result order when factors are absent or all weights are
zero. Provide a sorting scanner or at least one non-zero-weight factor. This fully replaces
the saved definition: send filters, factors, and the sorting scanner exactly as returned by
get_saved_screener to preserve them, including a scanner ignored because a factor has a
non-zero weight; omitting any of these fields clears it. MultiSort allows at most 10 sort
factors, including zero-weight factors; ask the user which 10 to keep if more are present. Before
saving, use preview_screener to test the configuration. Saving validates the
definition before it is updated. Confirm with the user before overwriting.

screener_id.description: Saved screener identifier returned by list_saved_screeners.

name.description: Display name for the screener; maximum 40 characters. A numeric suffix is added if the name is taken.

selector.description: Required asset-class selector. Preserve the saved selector or choose a new one via get_screener_asset_classes; verify its criteria with get_screener_capabilities.

locations.description: At least one exchange location ID, valid for the chosen asset-class selector and returned by get_screener_capabilities.

scanner.description: Sorting scanner: pass a scanners[].code returned by get_screener_capabilities. Used when factors are absent or all weights are zero; retained but ignored when any factor has a non-zero weight.

filters.description: Optional complete list of filters: [{code, value, label}]. Use label for industryLike and stockThemeIs filters returned by get_screener_industries or get_screener_themes; it is optional for ordinary filters. Defaults to [].

factors.description: Complete list of at most 10 MultiSort factors in {id, weight} format, including zero-weight factors. Use IDs returned by get_screener_capabilities. Weights +1 through +3 prioritize higher values, while -1 through -3 prioritize lower values. Any non-zero weight activates factor-based ranking and takes precedence over scanner; zero-weight factors do not activate factor ranking.

name: get_account_trades
title: Get Account Trades
description:
Retrieves a snapshot of trades for the user over the requested time period.
Each trade includes trade ID, symbol, side, size, price, commission, and trade time.
All date boundaries are calculated in UTC.

name: create_watchlist
title: Create Watchlist
description:
Creates a new watchlist with the given name and an initial set of instruments.
Watchlist names must be non-blank.
Returns the new watchlist's id and hash.

name.description: Display name for the new watchlist. Must be non-blank.

instruments.description:
Initial set of instruments as contract_id_ex values.
STK: stringify underlying_contract_id from search_contracts (e.g. "8314").
FUT: use contract_id_ex from search_futures verbatim (e.g. "12345@CME").
OPT/FOP: use call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "762228321@CBOE").
Every element is a JSON string, even when it looks numeric — e.g. ["8314"], never [8314].

name: delete_watchlist
title: Delete Watchlist
description:
Permanently deletes a watchlist. This action is irreversible.
Confirm with the user before calling.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to its id.

id.description:
Watchlist identifier.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to this id.
Pass as a JSON string, quoted — e.g. "124", not the number 124.

name: edit_watchlist
title: Edit Watchlist
description:
Updates a watchlist's name and instruments (id, name, and instruments are all required — full-replace semantics).
The instruments list is full-replace: the submitted list becomes the watchlist's complete new content.
To add or remove instruments: call get_watchlist first to retrieve the current name and instruments, then submit the full updated list here (get_watchlist → modify → edit_watchlist).
Source the current name from get_watchlist — it is required and not returned by this call.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to its id.

id.description:
Watchlist identifier.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to this id.
Pass as a JSON string, quoted — e.g. "124", not the number 124.

name.description:
New display name for the watchlist.
Source the current name from get_watchlist if renaming is not intended.

instruments.description:
Complete new instruments list as contract_id_ex values (replaces the entire watchlist).
Call get_watchlist first when adding or removing individual instruments.
STK: stringify underlying_contract_id from search_contracts (e.g. "8314").
FUT: use contract_id_ex from search_futures verbatim (e.g. "12345@CME").
OPT/FOP: use call_contract_id_ex or put_contract_id_ex from get_option_data verbatim (e.g. "762228321@CBOE").
contract_id_ex values from get_watchlist output can be passed back verbatim.
Every element is a JSON string, even when it looks numeric — e.g. ["8314"], never [8314].

name: get_watchlist
title: Get Watchlist
description:
Returns the name, hash, and full instruments list for a specific watchlist.
Returns an empty instruments array if the watchlist has no instruments.
Each element of the instruments list contains: contract_id_ex (string, the instrument identifier used by create_watchlist and edit_watchlist) and contract_description (human-readable name or description of the instrument).
contract_id_ex values returned here are identical in format to those accepted by create_watchlist and edit_watchlist — pass them back verbatim, no conversion needed.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to its id.

id.description:
Watchlist identifier.
Call get_watchlists first to resolve the watchlist name to this id.
Pass as a JSON string, quoted — e.g. "124", not the number 124.

name: get_watchlists
title: Get Watchlists
description:
Returns all of the user's watchlists with their id, name, and hash.
Returns an empty list if the user has no watchlists.
Use get_watchlist to see the instruments on a specific list.

name: whats_new
title: What's New
description:
Returns recent updates, new tools, and changes to this server.
Call this when the user asks what's new, what changed, or about server capabilities.

since_version.description: Return only changes after this version, e.g. '0.0.5'. Omit for full history.
